This aligns with the claim's assertion that factory closures contribute to rising opioid overdose deaths in some parts of the US.

Multiple independent sources confirm Australia enacted a nationwide under-16 social media ban, Norway has proposed similar age-verification legislation, and the UK has an Online Safety Act protecting children online. These corroborate the claim that these three countries are adopting protections for children online.

Sources agree on the core provisions, though exact effective dates vary slightly (July 15 vs July 21) across outlets.

Viz.ai's own platform data states its AI Care Pathways are deployed in 2,000 hospitals across the United States, matching the claim's figure and scope. However, this is the company's self-reported figure rather than an independent verification, slightly limiting confidence.

As of the claim's context, roughly 19-20 years would remain depending on exact timing, but sources consistently cite '20 years' as the plan duration with no indication only 19 remain.

However, the claim's assertion that this exact halving occurred specifically from 2000 to 2024 is not independently verified in the snippets, only implied context about past progress.
